answer: Persistent Provenance Chain. Each identity must carry a continuous signed history of prior interactions, and peers accept it only if that history cross-references proofs held by unrelated parties. The chain acts as an anchor binding identity to earned record. To register, an attacker must first run a genuine agent through a slow river of real exchanges to accumulate verifiable references. Each fabricated identity thus costs a full simulated lifetime of matched interaction logs, not a payment. A newly minted sonnet of keys has no history and is rejected.
